candidate_event_identifiers.declared_where: the request names them as candidates; the earlier audit of this host read them from the provider's own documentation and recorded their downstream meaning, but no record of this host was ever seen for any of them
candidate_event_identifiers.what_would_verify_them: one real record per identifier, read from a channel this host enables, quoted in data/st6/rfc047/EVENT_SEMANTICS.json together with its channel and its record id
candidate_event_identifiers.why_not: no record carrying any of these identifiers exists in a channel this session can read, so their meaning could not be verified against a real record and this RFC does not assign them one

permissions.source: the channel's channelAccess attribute, read from wevtutil gl

time_basis.reading: the newest record is not in the future, so the instants of this channel are UTC as they claim to be

permissions.source: the channel's channelAccess attribute, read from wevtutil gl

commands_run: wevtutil gl <channel>            (read a channel's own configuration)
wevtutil gli <channel>           (read how much of a log is still present)
wevtutil qe <channel> /f:xml ...  (read records; no filter writes anything)
wevtutil sl <channel> /e:true    (the gate; refused here without elevation)
coverage_reading: no instant exists from which a per-run record could exist: the operational channel is disabled and has never recorded on this host, so every slot of the period is outside the reach of external evidence, and a later rebuild may not promote one

activation_request.note: the change was requested with the exact command and the request for an elevated token was not approved in this session, so the change was not applied; the refusal of the unelevated attempt above is the measurement of the gate and is recorded rather than worked around

gate.change_contemplated: enable the Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Operational channel (wevtutil sl ... /e:true): the only configuration change RFC-047 contemplates

probe.reading: the host refused the change without an elevated token, which is the gate RFC-047 describes: it is recorded and not worked around

rollback.does_not: delete the evidence already collected, touch the Security channel, change any ACL, GPO, size limit, retention policy or any other administrator's configuration
rollback.restores: the channel's enabled flag to the value recorded above as state_before

purpose: the before-state of the audit channels, the permissions the effective user holds over them, the gate that stands between this session and the one configuration change RFC-047 contemplates, and how that change would be reversed

retention.circular_policy_means: the channel overwrites its oldest record rather than backing it up, so the system's own history cannot be the durable record; that is why this RFC persists what it reads
